The district was created ahead of the [[1969 Philippine House of Representatives elections|1969 House elections]] after the former Mountain Province was divided into the provinces of [[Benguet]], [[Mountain Province]], [[Ifugao]], and [[Kalinga-Apayao]] in 1966.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=4695|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/7121 |title=An Act Creating the Provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Ifugao and Kalinga-Apayao|date=June 18, 1966|accessdate=July 14, 2026}} It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] since the [[7th Congress of the Philippines|7th Congress]] from 1969 to 1972, in the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]], the unicameral parliament that replaced the House of Representatives from 1984 to 1986, and in the restored House from the [[8th Congress of the Philippines|8th Congress]] onwards. The district served as an electoral district in the [[Philippine Constitutional Convention of 1971|1971 Constitutional Convention]], with two delegates representing Ifugao at-large.{{Cite PH act|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/14108|chamber=RA|number=6132|date=August 24, 1970|title=An Act Implementing Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Two as Amended by Resolution of Both Houses Numbered Four of the Congress of the Philippines Calling for a Constitutional Convention, Providing for Proportional Representation Therein and Other Details Relating to the Election of Delegates to and the Holding of the Constitutional Convention, Repealing for the Purpose Republic Act Four Thousand Nine Hundred Fourteen, and for Other Purposes}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by Solomon Chungalao of the [[Nationalist People's Coalition]].{{Cite web |title=House Members - 20th Congress |url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/house-members |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]]}} == History == The district was first represented in the restored House by Gualberto Lumauig, the first [[governor of Ifugao]], who was elected in 1987 to the [[8th Congress of the Philippines|8th Congress]].{{Cite web |last=Cepeda |first=Mara |date=2018-11-19 |title=Ex-Ifugao congressman Gualberto Lumauig dies |url=https://www.rappler.com/philippines/217006-former-ifugao-congressman-gualberto-lumauig-dies/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[Rappler]] |language=en-US}} He was defeated in 1992 by incumbent governor Benjamin Cappleman, who served three consecutive terms until 2001.{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2006-11-04 |title=Ifugao has new governor |url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/19832/ifugao-has-new-governor/story/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[GMA News|GMA News Online]] |language=en}} Cappleman was succeeded by Solomon Chungalao, who also served for three consecutive terms until 2010. In 2010, Governor [[Teddy Baguilat]] was elected to the district's seat as a member of the [[Liberal Party (Philippines)|Liberal Party]].{{Cite web |last=Mendoza |first=John Eric |date=2021-10-08 |title=Ex-Rep. Teddy Baguilat files candidacy for senator |url=https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1499161/teddy-baguilat-files-candidacy-for-senator |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[Philippine Daily Inquirer]] |language=en}} He was later nominated in the [[List of Speaker of the Philippine House of Representatives elections#July 2016|2016 election for speaker]] but was defeated by [[Pantaleon Alvarez]] of [[PDP–Laban]].{{Cite web |date=2016-07-25 |title='Supermajority' backs Alvarez as House speaker |url=https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2016/07/25/1606483/supermajority-backs-alvarez-house-speaker |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=[[The Philippine Star]]}} Chungalao was re-elected in 2019 and subsequently won successive terms in 2022 and 2025.
